job.title: Local-First PDF Ingestion & Staging System (Python + Streamlit + SQLite)
job.description: We need a local-only PDF ingestion and staging tool that can accept PDF uploads via a simple local UI, de-duplicate files using SHA-256 hashing, extract text from each page using pdfplumber, run Tesseract OCR only on pages that contain no embedded text, and store file metadata and page text in a local SQLite database. This will be used for internal document processing workflows. No personal data extraction, API integration, or external services are required — this is ingestion only.
requirements: Accept PDF uploads via a simple local UI
Extract text from each page using pdfplumber
Run Tesseract OCR only on pages without embedded text
Store file metadata and page text in a local SQLite database

proposal.text:
Hello Andrew,

Your project aligns perfectly with work I’ve done before—most notably my Patent Similarity Analyzer, where I not only built the backend for PDF parsing and text extraction but also developed a full application for handling uploads, processing, and local storage.

Here’s how I can deliver your requirements:

Simple Local UI – A lightweight, intuitive interface for uploading PDFs, either via drag-and-drop or file selection.

De-duplication with SHA-256 – Prevents storing duplicate files by hashing uploads and checking against existing entries.

Smart Text Extraction – Use pdfplumber for embedded text and automatically run Tesseract OCR only on pages without text.

Local SQLite Database – Store file metadata (hash, filename, page count, upload date) and per-page text for easy search and indexing.

Offline-Only Operation – 100% local, no external API calls, ensuring privacy and security.

I will ensure the tool is:

Fast and reliable for processing multiple PDFs in sequence

Extensible, so you can add features like tagging, keyword search, or export later

Well-documented for easy maintenance

You can view my related project here: https://github.com/Adieltheanalyst/patent-similarity-analyzer

Let’s discuss your preferred UI framework (Tkinter, Streamlit, or a lightweight local web app) so I can build something that fits seamlessly into your workflow.

Best regards,
Adiel Ngugi
